title.narrative: Strengthening the resilience of vulnerable populations to climatic shocks in Somali region of Ethiopia

description.narrative: Ethiopia is vulnerable to frequent, multiple and often overlapping shocks that lead to a precarious food security, nutrition and livelihoods situation especially among the poorest segments of the population. The major climatic shocks driving annual needs in the country and specifically in Somali region are droughts and floods. The region is recovering from years of extreme drought and dry conditions that affected both crop and livestock production. Currently, the region is experiencing La Nina induced weather phenomenon, it has brought less rains and dry conditions especially for the extreme southern part of the region spilling into northern parts of Kenya. The proposed project is therefore aimed at saving lives of the most vulnerable households and communities by responding to the immediate humanitarian needs while at the same time strengthening their capacity to absorb and adapt to the frequent and cyclical climatic shocks they face. This project will be implemented in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Shebelle zone of Somali region. The IOM will provide early warning information based on their Transhumance Tracking Tool (TTT), which tracks the movement of pastoral communities in the face of a shock to inform FAO where to locate the water points to be rehabilitated. Overall, the project will directly benefit 17,610 people through the following interventions:Improving access to water for livestock in the drought prone areas: The project through this component will support the rehabilitation of two water points through a combination of cash for work and mechanized works. The Cash for Work scheme will provide income for 722 vulnerable households (3,610 individuals) to enable them meet their immediate needs. Each participating household will be paid USD 120 for 20 days' work during the rehabilitation process. Further, water points developed are estimated to improve access to water for livestock for 1,400 households (7,000 individuals) in the target areas. Therefore, the water access component of the project will benefit a total of 10,610 people (2,122 households). The location of the water points to be develop will be informed by the early warning information provided by IOM based on the Transhumance Tracking Tool (TTT). Provision and promotion of climate smart technologies and techniques: The recurrent climatic shocks in Somali region have affected food production especially among the most vulnerable resource constrained farmers. Therefore, the project will support the following interventions to strengthen the adaptability and resilience of farmers to climatic shocks.- Provision of improved seeds of climate resilient crop varieties - the support will focus on crops or varieties that exhibit enhanced tolerance to climatic shocks mainly drought and flood and can guarantee high yields under stress conditions. Further, FAO will provide seed types that can be recycled, and farmers will be trained to select and preserve seeds for future use. The project will provide climate resilient seeds to 7,000 people (1,400 households). In addition, each beneficiary household will receive a complementary unconditional cash of USD 100 to enable them to meet their immediate consumption and production needs including purchase of food, fertilizer, labor, etc. and mitigate the adoption of negative coping strategies.- Provision of tailor-made trainings on climate smart agriculture practices - the project will support the training of agricultural extension agents on climate smart agriculture and capacitate them to cascade the training to the beneficiaries. The skills and knowledge from the training and coaching sessions will help the target beneficiaries sustainably improve crop productivity thereby enhancing households’ adaptive capacities and resilience to climate changes. These activities are in line with the prioritized adaptation options for Somali region as espoused in the national adaptation plan.
